findings.severity_note: the arm's own log does not support the completed:true it is recorded with; repair by re-running the head population arm to a log that ends in a bare EXIT= line, or by correcting after_suite.completed.
findings.text: the head importer arm's log is truncated mid-run: its last line reads '...F' with no pytest summary line and no bare EXIT= line, yet the manifest records after_suite as completed:true, exit_status:1, failure_count:1, log_path importer-head.log. The receipt the record cites therefore cannot show the 76 passed/1 failed it claims, and the landed evidence fragment's own claim that every log 'ends in a bare EXIT= line' is false of this one. The figures do appear in the worker's own stream (stream.jsonl carries '1 failed, 76 passed in 183.22s'), and the base arm logs/importer-base.log is complete with a readable summary and EXIT=1, so the substance is corroborated, but the named artefact is not readable and promotion reads the EXIT= line from a log.

_append_bounded_log_line duplicates an owner the repository already has: reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:76 _append_crew_log_line is the declared shared crew-home log writer ('Both callers ... pass through here'), and the addition copies its body verbatim -- crew_home() parent mkdir, json.dumps(separators=(',',':'), default=str), one os.write on an O_APPEND descriptor, the same swallowed exception -- without calling or extending it. Only the trim is new, so the crew-home JSONL writer now exists twice and a change to one (locking, encoding, error policy) silently diverges from the other.

the measure paragraph opens 'Measure, all at revision 3b7793ab3', but the focused gate ran at the head: logs/focused-head.log's header reads '# rev 46b9411e99ff8f45d4cebf2723f14878b58ba997 tree <the reviewed worktree>', and importer-head.log's header names the same head with module_file under it. Only the base arm and the pre-commit negative control belong to 3b7793ab3, so the landed fragment cites the base revision for a measure taken at the head.

assert launched_pointer['allowance'] == 2 has the same-variable shape: the 2 is the worker_slots figure the test itself published into the lane document at line 220, so both sides move together and the assertion holds for any implementation that passes the published figure straight through, including one that never applies the held-versus-open decision. The sibling at line 254 does discriminate, because the code maps a held read to a literal 0 rather than echoing the input, and line 260's allowance_source compares against a string the test never supplies.
